title: Auth sign-in (split-screen)
summary: Production-grade sign-in page with optional social providers, remember-me, forgot-password link, and pluggable AuthAdapter for credential routing.
brief: Ship a sign-in page wired to my auth library — email + password with remember-me, optional GitHub/Google social buttons, forgot-password link, and a real error surface for failed sign-ins.

steps.reason: The page-level block — wires the form state, social handoff, error display, and pending state. Routes every credential call through the supplied AuthAdapter.
Accessible labels for email + password + remember-me
Submit + social CTAs (loading prop drives the busy state)
Inline error surface for failed sign-in
Visual divider between social and credential sections

checklist.check: Pass an AuthAdapter via the `adapter` prop. The block surfaces an 'unimplemented' error if the user submits without one — there is no built-in fallback.
Provide an `onSuccess` handler that navigates the user. The adapter's `redirect` field is informational; the block does not navigate by itself.
Adapter methods must return `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }` on failure (never throw). The block reads `error.message` into the Alert; thrown errors lose the structured payload.
socialProviders entries must be `{ provider, label, icon? }`. `provider` is forwarded verbatim to `adapter.signInWithSocial({ provider })`.
The left marketing panel is `aria-hidden` so SR users skip directly to the form. Don't put critical info there — duplicate any required text inside the form area.
[AuthSignInSplit] Avoid: Forgetting to pass the AuthAdapter — the block has no built-in fallback and will surface 'unimplemented' errors when the user submits.
[AuthSignInSplit] Avoid: Hard-coding signUpHref / forgotPasswordHref to absolute URLs — they're plain anchor hrefs, prefer in-app relative paths so the consumer's router handles navigation.
[AuthSignInSplit] Avoid: Skipping onSuccess and relying on adapter.redirect alone — the redirect is informational; the consumer's onSuccess handler is what actually navigates.

[AuthSignInSplit] Avoid: Wiring auth state inside the adapter methods instead of returning { ok, error } — the block reads the result and shows the error Alert; throwing inside the adapter loses the structured error payload.

[AuthSignInSplit] A11y: Form inputs have explicit Label htmlFor pairing, autoComplete='email' / 'current-password', and required attributes. Submit button uses the canonical loading prop (sets aria-busy + disabled). Errors render in an Alert with role='alert' so they're announced. Marketing aside is aria-hidden so screen-reader users don't traverse decorative copy before reaching the form.
[Form] Avoid: Forgetting to spread {...field} into the form control (connects value/onChange)
[Form] Avoid: Putting FormLabel outside FormItem (loses htmlFor wiring)
[Form] Avoid: Using useForm without a resolver when zod validation is desired
[Form] Avoid: Calling form.handleSubmit without a callback

[Form] A11y: FormControl automatically wires id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid. FormLabel uses htmlFor matching the control id. Errors are announced via FormMessage with matching aria-describedby.
[Label] Avoid: Forgetting to set htmlFor matching the input's id
[Label] Avoid: Using Label for non-form text content
[Label] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside Label
[Label] A11y: Clicking the label focuses the associated control. Automatically communicates the label to screen readers. Use htmlFor/id pairing, not nesting.
[Input] Avoid: Missing associated Label element for accessibility
[Input] Avoid: Using type='number' without min/max constraints
[Input] Avoid: Not providing placeholder text for context
[Input] A11y: Always pair with a Label using htmlFor/id. Consider aria-describedby for helper text or error messages.
[Checkbox] Avoid: Missing Label pairing
[Checkbox] Avoid: Using onChange instead of onCheckedChange
[Checkbox] Avoid: Forgetting that onCheckedChange can receive 'indeterminate' as well as boolean
[Checkbox] A11y: Always pair with Label via htmlFor/id. Radix handles aria-checked automatically.
[Button] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside asChild button
[Button] Avoid: Using — breaks middle-click, cmd-click, and right-click → 'open in new tab', and skips the browser history entry
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button variant='destructive'> for recoverable actions like 'Reset filters' — reserve destructive for delete/archive/leave; use 'secondary' or 'ghost' for resets
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button size='icon'> without an aria-label — screen readers have nothing to announce; always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label or visible text
[Button] A11y: Automatically handles focus ring, disabled state, and aria attributes. Icon-only buttons MUST have aria-label. Loading state automatically sets disabled.
[Alert] Avoid: Using destructive for non-error messages
[Alert] Avoid: Missing AlertTitle (reduces scannability)
[Alert] Avoid: Stacking multiple Alerts on the same page instead of grouping
[Alert] A11y: Root renders role='alert' so screen readers announce it. For non-urgent info banners consider role='status' or aria-live='polite' via className overrides.
[Separator] Avoid: Using as spacing instead of semantic separation
[Separator] Avoid: Forgetting orientation='vertical' needs parent height
[Separator] A11y: Set decorative=false if the separator conveys semantic meaning. Radix handles role='separator'.
